hints: Sketch the boundary circle $|z - (4 + 3\mathrm{i})| = 2$ with centre $(4, 3)$ and radius $2$.
Draw the half-line starting at $(2, 1)$ making an angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ with the positive real axis.
Shade the region inside/on the circle and on the side of the half-line where argument is $\geqslant \dfrac{\pi}{3}$.
walkthrough:
Identify the locus $|z - 4 - 3\mathrm{i}| \leqslant 2$:
Rewrite as $|z - (4 + 3\mathrm{i})| \leqslant 2$. This represents the closed circular disc with centre $C(4, 3)$ and radius $r = 2$.

Mark key boundary coordinates of the circle:
- Top: $(4, 3 + 2) = (4, 5)$
- Bottom: $(4, 3 - 2) = (4, 1)$
- Left: $(4 - 2, 3) = (2, 3)$
- Right: $(4 + 2, 3) = (6, 3)$

Identify the locus $\arg(z - 2 - \mathrm{i}) \geqslant \dfrac{\pi}{3}$:
Rewrite as $\arg(z - (2 + \mathrm{i})) \geqslant \dfrac{\pi}{3}$. This is the region bounded by a half-line starting at $P(2, 1)$ with direction angle $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ ($60^\circ$) to the positive real axis, including points rotated anticlockwise from this half-line.
Notice that the starting point $(2, 1)$ is vertically below the leftmost point of the circle $(2, 3)$, and the half-line passes through the top of the circle.
Shade the region on the Argand diagram representing the intersection of the circular disc and the half-line angular region.

hints: The maximum argument corresponds to the upper tangent from the origin $O(0, 0)$ to the circle $|z - (4 + 3\mathrm{i})| = 2$.
Use $\max\arg z = \arctan\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right) + \arcsin\left(\dfrac{2}{5}\right)$ to evaluate the angle in radians.
walkthrough:
Identify the point in the shaded region having greatest argument:
The argument $\arg z$ represents the angle from the positive real axis to the line segment $Oz$. Within the circular disc, the maximum argument occurs at the point of tangency of the upper tangent line drawn from the origin to the circle.

Verify that this upper tangent point lies in the shaded region:
The centre of the circle is $C(4, 3)$ with distance to the origin:
$$OC = \sqrt{4^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{16 + 9} = \sqrt{25} = 5$$

Calculate the angle of the centre line $OC$ with the positive real axis:
$$\alpha = \arctan\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right) \approx 0.6435011 \text{ radians}$$

In the right-angled triangle formed by the origin, the centre $C$, and the point of tangency, the radius $r = 2$ is opposite the angle $\beta$ between the tangent and $OC$:
$$\sin\beta = \dfrac{r}{OC} = \dfrac{2}{5} = 0.4$$
$$\beta = \arcsin(0.4) \approx 0.4115168 \text{ radians}$$

Sum the two angles to find the greatest argument:
$$\max\arg z = \alpha + \beta = \arctan\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right) + \arcsin\left(\dfrac{2}{5}\right)$$
$$\max\arg z \approx 0.6435011 + 0.4115168 = 1.0550179 \dots \approx 1.06 \text{ radians}$$
$$\left(\text{or approximately } 60.5^\circ\right)$$
